A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite revisions to the multivariate theory and pagination.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.3 report original synthetic-data experiments, including network sparsity during training and learned interpolants in Figures 3 and 17–20.

after.justification: V3 retains the original synthetic-data training experiments and their sparsity curves and learned interpolants in Section 5 and Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: The formal multivariate optimization in Equations (8)–(11) drops the explicit infinity-norm constraints on weight products and reformulated variables. This relaxes the proposed formulation, while the path-norm penalty, network architecture and implemented reweighted algorithm remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six-point univariate peak/plateau dataset and ten synthetic points in 50 dimensions, with coordinates and labels sampled uniformly from [-1, 1]. No evaluated task or scenario is added.

E2.justification: Both experiments retain unregularized Adam and AdamW as comparators, alongside reweighted regularization with p = 0.4, 0.7 and 1. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3.2 retains MSE training for 100,000 epochs, learning rate 0.01, widths 80 and 100, and regularization parameters 0.003 and 0.005 for the respective datasets. The theoretical constraint removal is not reported as a change to these experiments.

E4.justification: The comparisons across p values and the learned-function snapshots throughout training in Figure 19 are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis or case study appears.

E5.justification: Both versions document shared random initialization for the univariate comparison. Neither reports repeated-run counts, numerical seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 3 and 17–20 retain identical plotted results and learned interpolants. Both report that p = 0.4 recovers the three-neuron univariate solution and that all tested p values produce multivariate solutions satisfying the 2N sparsity bound.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds existence proofs, extends Proposition 4.1's N-neuron bound to every 0 < p < 1, and proves p-independent boundedness, allowing Theorem 4.1 to dispense with an imposed weight bound. Lemma 4.1 now uses realizable activation patterns and explicitly bounds the number of nonzero neuron blocks. V2's Remark 2 extending the result to piecewise-linear loss objectives is removed.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution 2 strengthens the central multivariate guarantee by removing the explicit weight-boundedness restriction and extending the N-neuron guarantee from sparsest solutions to all ℓp minimizers for 0 < p < 1. The principal univariate claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4 replaces the discussion of required weight bounds with remaining limitations concerning functional structure, uniqueness and equivalence to ℓ1 minimization. It also withdraws the stated extensions to unregularized biases and piecewise-linear loss objectives. Experimental interpretations and the difficulty of efficiently computing p* are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 retains Algorithm 1, its balancing convention, PyTorch/Adam implementation information, experimental hyperparameters and the same code-access link. No implementation or resource-access information is added.

R1.justification: V3 credits Yang, Chen and Xiang (2022a) for the boundedness argument and adds Cover for the activation-pattern bound. It removes the corresponding Ojha, Winder and Stanley citations. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 corrects typographical errors and notation, changes appendix references from 'Section' to 'Appendix', and organizes the multivariate proofs into named steps. The overall section structure and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: All twenty figures retain their graphics, axes and legends. Limited caption edits, split equation displays and changes in figure placement relative to surrounding text alter the layout, particularly in the experimental appendix.

improvement.justification: The new arguments in Appendix A.2 remove an important restriction on the central multivariate theorem and establish existence and an all-p neuron bound that v2 lacked. These substantially strengthen the theoretical foundation and justified applicability of the paper. Withdrawal of the bias/loss extensions narrows secondary scope, and the empirical evidence is unchanged, but the central theoretical gains support a substantial overall improvement.
